chapter: Rose Murphy, wartime 52nd Street, Town Hall
title: Secretly recorded by Rosenkrantz and never paid royalties
summary: The audience cheered, then Rosenkrantz revealed he had taped them; the Commodore release was a big seller but they got no royalties.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: And that went over -- we finished out, finally finished the number, and the audience stood up and gave us such a round of applause, you know. It was so wonderful. Then, of course, we did another number which was called "I've Got Rhythm," and that was it. That lasted for at least -- it could have lasted for about 20 -- almost a half hour. And that was very successful. I mean, they just gave us every welcome you could imagine, you know. But come to find out, after the show had finished, we got through the show all right, but after the show had finished, Timmie Rosenkrantz, the boss, so to speak, he comes up to us and tells us what a great job that we did and everybody just loved us all the way. At the same time, he was trying to get to the point of telling us that, "You know, I happen to be able to record you," he had a little tape recorder backstage, and he was recording us all this time, which we didn't know.
But then, after he had told us that, he says, "You will be compensated for it," and what have you, which was good news at that time. So anyway, come to find out

this recording before long had come out -- it had been reproduced for the market, you know, and it was a big seller, those two numbers, especially "I've Got Rhythm," on record. I think it was on Commodore.
Oh, yeah, so they put it out then around that time?
And did you all get any royalties?
We never did get any royalties. The only -- in fact, we were only paid for the concert itself on top of the fact that he said we would be compensated.
I guess he meant historical compensation.
So what could we possibly do? Anyway, that became a big hit, record-wise. And so, I guess people are still listening to it now and then.
